summary: No trades. The account is about 88.6% invested (cash $70.61, 11.4%), inside the 80-90% target, so only about $9 sits above the 10% buffer, and L4 rules out a token-sized buy justified only by diversification. The Market Analyst is risk-off at confidence 0.42 with SPY 0.77% above its 200-day line after the worst Nasdaq day since 2020, and the October payrolls print is a rates unknown, so I would not add risk into it. No held invalidation has tripped (checked against the latest marks implied by portfolio.json: IDXX about $660 vs $630 stop; DPZ about $334 vs $285; VRSN about $309 vs $278; BND $71.54 vs $70.0; IEF $91.83 vs $89.5; MSM about $111.9 vs about $108; SPY 733.00 vs 723.99 for VOO and VTI). BTC/USD is the exception to watch: the mark of about $75.5k (position value / qty) is only about 0.3% above the roughly $75.3k stop (10% under the $83,686 fill), and the 11-05 close of $75,972 is 0.9% above it; the invalidation is a close more than 10% below the fill and no close has been below it, and the exchange-failure and adverse-regulation clause has not tripped per the News Analyst (CLARITY Act rewrite is reports only, not enacted). I am not spending a slot on selling a 2% position on a stop that is intact, but if the next close is below $75.3k it should be sold in full (fraction 1.0) and re-anchoring is the Portfolio Manager's call. CARG's 11-05 print was a beat with a $250M buyback and a slightly soft Q4 sales guide (News Analyst, mixed-to-positive on numbers); the position is up on the fill, so the 'negative surprise' sell clause is not tripped on the numbers, though the price reaction is not in my inputs. Applied L1 (stops anchored to fills), L2 (earnings dates read from the News Analyst's per-name checks), L3 (DPZ, WMT, KR stack is about 26% by Staples label so no more staples), L4 (declined a token diversification buy) and L5 (reviewed every held name, with a lower-mark check on BTC and the SPY line). The PM asked for a named non-Technology, non-Staples candidate: when cash rises above the buffer, the first call is INCY (Health Care, F-score 8/9, gp_sector_pct 0.91, cfo $1.41B vs net income $1.29B, vol 0.33, no earnings until 2027-02-09, Fundamentals Analyst rank 8 with the one-time CMS $246M benefit caveat), ahead of adding to the book's US-equity beta; it would overlap IDXX in Health Care, and the Market Analyst favors Health Care, so I would size it small (about $9-10) and not today. I did not choose bonds because the NFP print is a two-way duration risk and BND, IEF are already about 9% of equity, nor GLD because it is 8.78% below its 200-day.
